excerpt: Add the tools you need (to-dos, message boards, chat, a calendar, card tables), then invite co-workers, clients, even AI Agents.
Message Boards replace email. Announcements and discussions live as posts, with every reply attached right below.
Make a list, or ten lists. Assign items, set due dates, attach files, even create subtasks.
Basecamp’s Hill Charts let you know exactly where things really stand.
Perfect for bug and issue tracking, software development, production work, or anything with distinct stages.
With Basecamp you don’t need Slack, WhatsApp, or another chat app. Just chat in Basecamp instead.
A global calendar brings every project together, and you can subscribe in Outlook, Google Calendar, HEY Calendar, and more.
Basecamp asks your team questions on a schedule, like “What are you working on this week?” every Monday at 9am, and saves everyone’s answers in one place.
Docs & Files keeps images, documents, PDFs, even cloud files from Figma, Google Docs, and Dropbox neatly organized inside your projects.
It’s keyboard accessible too, so you can pop your assignments up without touching the mouse.
A real game changer, Everything Views pull everything of one type onto a single page, no matter which project it’s in.
See overlaps, see beginnings and ends, see who’s on what, even see key dates superimposed over everything.
Hit `SHIFT` and little keys appear next to everything you can navigate to.
Basecamp’s Client mode lets you decide what they should — and shouldn’t — see, project by project.
Create reusable project and to-do list templates with the same structure, workflows, and setup across projects.
Track hours/time spent working on projects.
Official Basecamp support for ChatGPT, Claude, and AI agents with full MCP support.
**One project, free forever.** Invite up to 3 people.
With Basecamp, cancellation is entirely self-serve, no questions asked, no retention specialists
**AI agents** — Install the [Basecamp Skills](https://github.com/basecamp/skills) or the [Basecamp CLI](https://github.com/basecamp/basecamp-cli).
The OpenAPI spec and this REST API reference cover authentication, pagination, and every endpoint in detail.
You can access any resource directly without including its project (bucket) in the URL:
OAuth 2.0 allows users to authorize your application to use Basecamp on their behalf without having to copy/paste API tokens or touch sensitive login information.
Throughout the Basecamp API docs, we include "Copy as cURL" examples.
The Basecamp API also provides the `X-Total-Count` header, which displays the total number of resources in the collection you are fetching.
If the resource hasn't changed since your last request, you'll get a `304 Not Modified` response with no body, saving you the time and bandwidth of sending something you already have.
Consult the `Retry-After` response header to determine how long to wait (in seconds) before retrying the request.
To download a file, make an authenticated `GET` request to its `download_url` and follow the redirect.
Rich text content may contain lists, block quotes, simple formatting, and inline attachments such as mentions, images, and files.

Long-time user since version 1 says Basecamp got worse and more overpriced with every release. They recently signed up again to evaluate it for a team and found it "barely more useful than a piece of paper." They acknowledge its success suggests otherwise but say they don't understand it.

User who used Basecamp for a couple of years at a previous job, on a team of five, says they never found it particularly "snappy." They question the claims that it is fast without much client-side UI.
Critique of Basecamp Next's 'Stacker' navigation UI: it feels like breadcrumbs that take up more screen real estate than necessary. The commenter's first reaction was "this is just bread crumbs."
